_comment: Maps job-description text to input/master-resume-{track}.md files. Authoritative for which track files exist: a track absent from 'tracks' has no file and cannot be selected. Read at Step 2 in the same batch as the JD, applied at Step 3.

rules.matching: Case-insensitive, on word boundaries, never bare substring. 'erp' must not match inside 'enterprise', and 'ai' must not match inside 'maintain'. A multi-word entry matches as a phrase.
rules.order: Check no_fit first, then titles, then keyword scoring.
rules.step_1_no_fit: If any no_fit keyword appears in the JD title or must-haves, use no_fit.fallback_track as primary with no secondary, log no_fit.log, and stop.
rules.step_2_title: Match the JD job title against each track's 'titles'. The first hit is the PRIMARY. Do not stop here: the secondary still comes from step 3.
rules.step_3_secondary: If the primary declares a 'default_secondary', use it. Otherwise score every other track by counting its 'keywords' present in the JD's must-haves, and take the highest scorer that has at least min_keyword_hits. If none reaches it, run with the primary alone.
rules.step_4_no_title_match: If no title matched, score all tracks the same way, apply domain_boost, and the highest score is primary. Add a second only if its score is at least secondary_threshold times the primary's.
rules.primary_supplies: headline, summary, skill category ordering, and every fact in the output

caveats.log: Not recorded in any track file. devops is the closest track, but claim none of this. Would need real infrastructure work added to Section 5 to support it.

No named ERP or CRM vendor platform is recorded, only generic ERP and accounting integration over REST APIs and scheduled data exchange. Add the real platform names to Section 1 if the candidate has used them.
AI and LLM tooling is itemised in Section 1 but has no delivery project recorded against it in Section 5. Keep claims at the skill level, never at the project level, until a real project is added.

domain_boost._comment: The record has real healthcare delivery behind these three tracks, so a healthcare posting should favour them.

global_caveats.log: Record supports 7+ years, March 2019 to present. Do not inflate the headline or summary. If the JD makes the year count a hard bar, log it as a structural mismatch.
No LinkedIn or GitHub URL is recorded in Sections 8 and 9, so those fields are omitted from the contact line. Add real URLs to every track file to close this.

no_fit._comment: No track file covers these. Use fallback_track as primary, generate honestly from what the record holds, and log the mismatch at Step 8.
no_fit.log: JD is outside every track the record covers. Generated from master-resume-fs.md as the general software engineering fallback.

examples._comment: The 'jd' field is a short label, not the text matched against. The primary comes from the title, but the secondary is scored against the whole posting body, so these secondaries assume a full JD mentioning the relevant keywords.
